title: Thumbikin
year_evidence: この電子版は版年を刻んでいない
text:
Once on a time there was a woman who had an only son, and he was no
taller than your thumb; and so they called him Thumbikin.

Now, when he had come to be old enough to know right and wrong, his
mother told him to go out and woo him a bride, for now she said it was
high time he thought about getting a wife. When Thumbikin heard that,
he was very glad; so they got their driving gear in order and set off,
and his mother put him into her bosom. Now they were going to a palace
where there was an awfully big Princess, but when they had gone a bit
of the way, Thumbikin was lost and gone. His mother hunted for him
everywhere, and bawled to him, and wept because he was lost, and she
couldn’t find him again.

“_Pip, Pip_”, said Thumbikin, “here I am”; and he had hidden himself in
the horse’s mane.

So he came out, and had to give his word to his mother that he wouldn’t
do so any more. But when they had driven a bit further on, Thumbikin
was lost again. His mother hunted for him, and called him, and wept;
but gone he was, and gone he stayed.

“_Pip, Pip_”, said Thumbikin at last; and then she heard how he laughed
and tittered, but she couldn’t find him at all for the life of her.

“_Pip, Pip_, why, here I am now!” said Thumbikin, and came out of the
horse’s ear.

So he had to give his word that he wouldn’t hide himself again; but
they had scarce driven a bit further before he was gone again. He
couldn’t help it. As for his mother, she hunted, and wept, and called
him by name; but gone he was, and gone he stayed; and the more she
hunted, the less she could find him in any way.

“_Pip, Pip_, here I am then”, said Thumbikin.

But she couldn’t make out at all where he was, his voice sounded so
dull, and muffled.

So she hunted, and he kept on saying, “Pip, here I am”, and laughed and
chuckled, but she couldn’t find him; but all at once the horse snorted,
and it snorted Thumbikin out, for he had crept up one of his nostrils.

Then his mother took him and put him into a bag; she knew no other way,
for she saw well enough he couldn’t help hiding himself.

So, when they came to the palace, the match was soon made, for the
Princess thought him a pretty little chap, and it wasn’t long before
the wedding came on too.

Now, when they were going to sit down to the wedding-feast, Thumbikin
sat at the table by the Princess’s side; but he had worse than no seat,
for when he was to eat he couldn’t reach up to the table; and so if the
Princess hadn’t helped him up on to it, he wouldn’t have got a bit to
eat.

Now it went good and well so long as he had to eat off a plate, but
then there came a great bowl of porridge—that he couldn’t reach up to;
but Thumbikin soon found out a way to help himself; he climbed up and
sat on the lip of the bowl. But then there was a pat of melting butter
right in the middle of the bowl, and that he couldn’t reach to dip his
porridge into it, and so he went on and took his seat at the edge of
the melting butter; but just then who should come but the Princess,
with a great spoonful of porridge to dip it into the butter; and, alas!
she went too near to Thumbikin, and tipped him over; and so he fell
over head and ears, and was drowned in the melted butter.

So she hunted, and he kept on saying, “Pip, here I am”, and laughed and chuckled, but she couldn’t find him; but all at once the horse snorted, and it snorted Thumbikin out, for he had crept up one of his nostrils.
Then his mother took him and put him into a bag; she knew no other way, for she saw well enough he couldn’t help hiding himself.
So, when they came to the palace, the match was soon made, for the Princess thought him a pretty little chap, and it wasn’t long before the wedding came on too.

Now, when they were going to sit down to the wedding-feast, Thumbikin sat at the table by the Princess’s side; but he had worse than no seat, for when he was to eat he couldn’t reach up to the table; and so if the Princess hadn’t helped him up on to it, he wouldn’t have got a bit to eat.

むかしむかし、ひとり息子を持つ女がいて、その子はあなたの親指ほどの背丈もなかった。そこでみなはその子をおやゆびと呼んでいた。

さて、善悪のわかる年頃になると、母はその子に、出かけて花嫁を求めてこいと言った。そろそろ妻を持つことを考えるべき時分だというのである。おやゆびはそれを聞いてたいそう喜んだ。そこで二人は馬車の支度を整えて出発し、母はその子を懐に入れた。さて二人はたいそう大きな姫のいる宮殿へ行くことになっていた。ところが道を少し行くと、おやゆびがいなくなってしまった。母はあちこち探し回り、大声で呼び、いなくなって見つからないので泣いた。
「ぴぴっ」とおやゆびは言った。「ここにいるよ。」。馬のたてがみに隠れていたのである。
そこで彼は出てきて、母にもう二度としないと約束させられた。ところがもう少し行くと、おやゆびはまたいなくなった。母は探し、呼び、泣いた。だがいなくなったきり、いなくなったままだった。
「ぴぴっ」ととうとうおやゆびは言った。すると母には彼が笑ってくすくす言っているのが聞こえたが、どうしても見つけられなかった。
「ぴぴっ、ほら、ここにいるよ!」とおやゆびは言って、馬の耳から出てきた。
そこで彼はもう二度と隠れないと約束させられた。ところがもう少し行くか行かないかのうちに、また消えてしまった。どうにも堪えられなかったのである。母はといえば、探し、泣き、名を呼んだ。だがいなくなったきり、いなくなったままだった。そして探せば探すほど、どうしても見つからなかった。
「ぴぴっ、ここにいるよ」とおやゆびは言った。
だが母にはどこにいるのかまるでわからなかった。その声はひどくこもって鈍く聞こえたのである。
そこで母は探し、彼は「ぴぴっ、ここにいるよ」と言いつづけ、笑ってくすくす言ったが、母には見つけられなかった。ところが突然、馬が鼻を鳴らして、おやゆびを鼻から吹き出した。鼻孔の一つに這い込んでいたのである。
そこで母は彼を取って袋に入れた。ほかに手立てを知らなかったのである。隠れずにはいられない子なのだと、よくよく見て取ったからだ。
そうして宮殿に着くと、縁談はすぐにまとまった。姫は彼を可愛らしい小さな若者だと思ったのである。そして婚礼もまもなく行われた。
さて婚礼の宴の席につこうというとき、おやゆびは姫のかたわらの食卓についた。だが席がないも同然だった。食べようにも卓に手が届かなかったのである。そこで姫が卓の上に上げてやらなかったら、ひと口も食べられなかったろう。

さて皿から食べているうちはうまくいった。ところが大きな粥の鉢が出てくると、それには手が届かなかった。だがおやゆびはまもなく手立てを見つけた。よじ登って鉢の縁に坐ったのである。ところが鉢の真ん中には溶けたバターの塊があって、それには手が届かず、粥を浸せなかった。そこで彼は進んでいって、溶けたバターの縁に腰を下ろした。ところがちょうどそのとき、やって来たのは誰だったか。姫が匙に山盛りの粥をバターに浸そうとしていたのである。そして、ああ! 姫はおやゆびに近寄りすぎて、彼を突き落としてしまった。そこで彼は真っ逆さまに落ちて、溶けたバターで溺れ死んだ。
